title: stochastic-output-stability-harness-for-quantized-json-fncall-validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reproducible test harness that evaluates structured JSON/function-call outputs under stochastic perturbations that emulate FP8/INT8 calibration noise, KV-cache decay, and micro-batching ordering effects. The harness will run per-model profile sweeps and produce a summarized pass/fail matrix keyed by schema rules, token-level repairability, and probabilistic acceptance thresholds. This ticket covers design, implementation of the simulator, integration with the model calibration metadata store, CI gating, and initial rollout against 5 representative models (gptx-small-rl, redwood-mini, redwood-moderate, community-3B, community-13B).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can replay 3 seeded perturbation modes (quantization noise, KV decay, ordering jitter) against saved deterministic prompts and produce schema-validation metrics (JSON-schema pass rate, top-1 field mismatch rate, repairable field count). 2) CI job runs within 10 minutes on PRs and fails the PR if schema pass rate drops below per-model threshold (configurable). 3) Results are stored to /dashboards/quantization-stability and include diff snippets and sample tokens. 4) Runbook and follow-ups documented in confluence link provided.
design_notes: We will avoid purely synthetic noise: use calibration snapshots exported from runtime-1.20 (per-batch scale, dynamic range histograms) to parameterize Gaussian and heteroscedastic noise models. Simulate KV-cache 'staleness' by randomly truncating recent KV frames and replaying prefix continuations. Validation will be schema-aware — if a field fails, compute minimal token edits to reach conformance and mark as 'repairable' or 'irrecoverable'. Use probabilistic thresholds (e.g., 95th percentile sample pass) instead of absolute counts to reduce brittle CI flakes.
test_plan: - Curate a 300-prompt sample set stratified by length, function complexity, and expected schema branching. - Sweep FP8 and INT8 profiles with 3 calibration seeds each. - For each run compute: JSON-schema pass rate, per-field token divergence, top-3 repair suggestions, and latency impact. - Export results as NDJSON blobs and aggregate into a CI dashboard. - Include two 'stress' jobs as daily nightlies with 2k prompts to catch regressions.
implementation_steps: 1) Implement perturbation simulator module (python) with config-driven noise models. 2) Hook simulator into existing structured-output test runner. 3) Add model-profile loader that pulls calibration histograms from s3://redwood-calib-snapshots. 4) Implement schema repair estimator using token-level edit distance and rerank via small LM. 5) Add CI job and dashboard exporter. 6) Run baseline sweep and tune per-model thresholds. 7) Document runbook and failure triage steps.
ci_integration: New GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/quant-stability.yml. Runs a fast sweep (300 prompts x 3 seeds) on feature branches with a 10-minute budget (sampled). If the PR job reports a drop > configured delta or schema pass rate below threshold the job sets a failing status. Nightly workflows use the full 2k prompt suite and publish to dashboards/quantization-stability with historical retention of 90 days.
risks: - CI flakiness from nondeterministic model seeds; mitigated by fixed RNG seeds and percentile-based acceptance. - Simulation divergence from real runtime behavior if calibration snapshot sampling is biased. - Performance cost: repair estimator may add latency; we will run repair scoring offline and only include result summaries in PR checks.
comments: 2025-01-12: Spike complete. Prototype sampler and simple JSON-schema validator implemented. Observed that truncation of KV frames causes most schema failures for deeply nested function outputs.

2025-01-20: Architecture review with PM and QE. Decided to include repairability scoring and to parameterize thresholds per-model. PM requests export of example failure diff snippets for feature teams.
2025-01-28: UX/console team suggested linking failures to per-route historic cost/latency — accepted as follow-up (separate ticket).
2025-02-01: First CI workflow pushed to feature branch. Two failing PRs revealed calibration snapshot mismatch; created ENG-74600 to standardize snapshot format.
2025-02-02: Tuned per-model thresholds after baseline sweep; rolling mainline nightlies scheduled.
notes: Follow-ups: 1) Create a lightweight runtime hook to export calibration metadata in canonical format (ENG-74600). 2) Product to review schema pass thresholds for customer-facing models. 3) Explore automated rollback policy integration with rollouts if schema pass drops on production (requires safety review).
